quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should bend slightly at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests for better balance.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if the pass was started before the no passing zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must stay within the posted speed limit and only happen where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When should your rearview mirror be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Adjust them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep your speed steady or speed up gradually through the turn.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Passing and being passed when riding a motorcycle is not much different than when driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
A motorcycle's visibility is not as important as that of a car.
Passing should be done on the shoulder instead of on the main roadway.
It is critical to make eye contact with the other driver when riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
questions.explanation: The basic passing techniques are the same, but visibility matters more for motorcycles. Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss. A driver may not see you even if they look, or you could disappear into their blind spot.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure all loads so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: If you are riding in the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are likely riding in the best position to be seen.
You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
The driver will most likely assume you are there.
You are discouraging other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirrors, so this position helps them see you better.

questions.question: At night, should you follow other vehicles at a longer or shorter distance than during the day?

options.text: Keep a longer following distance at night.
Keep a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance day or night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is hard to see distances in the dark. You lose visual clues like shadows and light. At night, keep a longer following distance than you would during the day.

questions.question: What gives a rider the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Which of these items best protects a motorcyclist?

options.text: Shoes that do not cover the ankle

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Wear tall, sturdy boots that cover your ankles with low heels. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: Why check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: Only a mechanic can find problems.
You should not check it before riding.
You should only check it after riding.
It helps find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Limit how far you ride in one day

questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks on long trips. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to stay warm and dry. Never take artificial stimulants. When they wear off, the effects can be dangerous.

questions.question: How should a group of riders enter a highway?
questions.explanation: Normally, riders use a staggered formation. But when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway, use a single-file line.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When braking, use:

options.text: Either front or rear, but not both

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: What does a yellow sign with black lettering or symbols mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To lean your motorcycle for a turn, press:

options.text: The handgrip in the direction of the turn
The handgrip opposite the direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: The handgrip in the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help lower the chance of a crash?

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible to other drivers. Signal your intentions clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead for hazards and be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: As part of your normal routine.
They are not helpful since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your normal routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular scanning. Always check mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you as you turn. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of a proper lane position?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind, blind spots, and road hazards. It shows other drivers you are using your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears. Lane position does not help you avoid traffic signals.
